 ORDER

This FIRST bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.226/2023 registered at Police Station-Sironj, District- Vidisha (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 343,
376/34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, 2012.
Applicant is in judicial custody since 12.08.2023.

A s per the case of prosecution, Bablu Yadav, father of prosecutrix reported to Police Station Sironj,
District Vidisha that his daughter aged around 15 years is missing since the night of 12.06.2023.
He has apprehension that Abhishek Panthi has allured and taken his minor daughter.

On such allegation, FIR in Crime No.226 of 2023 for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC was Chotu@Gujjar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69326028/

sentences.text: During investigation, the victim was recovered on production by her parents on 19.06.2023.
She was forwarded to medico legal examination and her statement was recorded under Section 161 of CrPC.
Victim has alleged that she was taken to Gujarat by Abhishek, where Abhishek married to her at temple and, thereafter, committed rape on her.
Accordingly, an offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 343, 376/34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act was registered.
Abhishek was arrested.

On further investigation, it was revealed that present applicant Chotu @
Gujjar aided in taking of victim on 12.06.2022, therefore, he is also implicated in the present matter.
Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant has falsely been implicated in the matter.
The applicant is in custody since 12.08.2023.
The applicant is aged about 20 years.
He is pursuing his studies.
There is no likelihood of his absconding leaving the family behind to suffer.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Main accused Abhishek is arrested.
The applicant is permanent resident of Sironj, District Vidisha.
There is no likelihood of his absconding or interfering with investigation or evidence.
Jail incarceration is causing financial hardship to the family of the applicant.
Charge-sheet has been filed.
No further custodial interrogation is required.
The trial would take time to complete.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that co- accused persons, namely, Neelu Panthi and Preeti Bai have been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide orders dated 29/08/2023 and 05/09/2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.38459/2023 and M.Cr.C.No. 39668/2023 respectively and co-accused Umesh Ahirwar has been granted regular bail by this Court vide order dated 26.09.2023 in MCRC No.43214 of 2023.
The allegation against the applicant is identical.
On the ground of parity, the applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel contends that in her statement under Sections 161 and 164 of CrPC, the victim has alleged involvement of applicant in her kidnapping.
Therefore, the applicant may not be extended the benefit of bail.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that the applicant Chotu @ Gujjar shall be released on bail in connection with Crime No.226/2023 registered at Police Station Sironj, District Vidisha (M.P.), for an offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 343, 376/34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rs.
Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, for compliance with the following conditions, :
